mainTopic: מיאון: how it is done and written, how strong a minor's marriage is, and how מיאון differs from a גט
overview: The amud begins by finishing the rule for writing a שטר מיאון: keep it short so it is never mistaken for a גט. A ברייתא then defines which words count as מיאון, and רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי בר יהודה widen it to more and more surprising situations. The גמרא rules like רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס and brings רבי יהודה בן בתירה's teaching that a girl's marriage or betrothal to another man is itself her מיאון. After a chain of questions and the story of אבדן's daughters-in-law, the הלכה follows him, even if she had been fully married to the first husband. Next, שמואל praises רבי אלעזר for treating a minor's marriage consistently. In a ברייתא, רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע give opposite pictures of such a marriage, and רבי prefers רבי אליעזר. The גמרא then defines רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's 'obstruction from the man' in two ways. Finally, a new משנה contrasts מיאון with a גט and teaches that the way she left him last decides whether she may return to him.

steps.title: Keep the refusal document short so it is not mistaken for a divorce
steps.stepSummary: A long, detailed שטר מיאון could be confused with a גט, so חז״ל fixed a short, plain wording for it.
steps.simpleTranslation: A detailed refusal document might get mixed up with a bill of divorce. So they decreed this wording: 'On such-and-such a day, so-and-so, daughter of so-and-so, refused in our presence.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its discussion of how to write a שטר מיאון and gives the fixed short wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the document were written with the full language of a woman leaving her husband, someone might later use that wording as a גט. To prevent this, the document only records the fact that she refused, on a certain day, in front of witnesses.

keyTerms.meaning: It may come to be confused (mixed up)
In our presence (literally, before our faces)

steps.whatToRemember: A שטר מיאון only states that she refused, on a certain day, in front of witnesses. Nothing more, so it never looks like a גט.

phrases.english: It may come to be confused with a bill of divorce.
phrases.notes: The 'it' is the refusal document the גמרא was just discussing.

phrases.english: They decreed as follows:
'On such-and-such a day, so-and-so refused,
the daughter of so-and-so, in our presence.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the discussion that began before this section about the wording of the שטר מיאון.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The שטר מיאון uses a short, fixed wording so that it cannot be mixed up with a גט.

steps.title: What words count as a refusal
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא defines מיאון: the girl says she does not want her husband, or does not want the קידושין her mother and brothers arranged.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: What is a refusal? If she said, 'I do not want so-and-so my husband,' or 'I do not want the betrothal that my mother and brothers arranged for me.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that explains what a girl has to say for it to count as מיאון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מיאון is done with words, not with a document or a ceremony. Two basic wordings work: rejecting the husband himself, or rejecting the קידושין her relatives made for her.

keyTerms.meaning: Refusal: a young girl leaving a marriage her relatives arranged

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
What is a refusal?
If she said: 'I do not want so-and-so my husband,'
or: 'I do not want the betrothal
that my mother and my brothers betrothed me with.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the wording of the document to the wording of the refusal itself.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Saying 'I do not want my husband' or 'I do not want the betrothal my mother and brothers made' counts as מיאון.

steps.title: Refusing even on the way to the wedding
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says that even if she says it while being carried to her husband's house, it counts as מיאון.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה went further: Even if she is sitting in the bridal carriage on the way from her father's house to her husband's, and she says 'I do not want so-and-so my husband,' that is a refusal.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה widens the rule: מיאון works even in the middle of the wedding procession.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might think that once she is on the way to the wedding, the process has gone too far for her to back out. רבי יהודה teaches that it has not; her words still count as מיאון.

phrases.aramaic: יָתֵר עַל כֵּן אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda said more than that:
Even if she is sitting in a bridal carriage
and going from her father's house to her husband's house,
and she said: 'I do not want so-and-so my husband'
this is a refusal.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָתֵר עַל כֵּן אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the basic definition to a later, more committed stage.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Words of refusal said during the wedding procession still count as מיאון.

steps.title: Refusing even while serving guests in his house
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה goes further: even while serving drinks to guests in her husband's home, her words count as מיאון.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה went even further: Even if guests were reclining in her husband's house and she was standing and serving them drinks, and she said to them, 'I do not want so-and-so my husband,' it is a refusal.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה widens the rule again, now to when she is already living in her husband's house and acting as his wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here she might just be complaining about the hard work of serving guests, so you might not take her words seriously. Still, רבי יהודה says her words count as real מיאון.

phrases.aramaic: יָתֵר עַל כֵּן אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda said more than that:

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ הָיוּ אוֹרְחִין מְסוּבִּין בְּבֵית בַּעְלָהּ
phrases.english: Even if guests were reclining at her husband's house
and she is standing and serving them drinks,
and she said to them: 'I do not want so-and-so my husband'
this is a refusal.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָתֵר עַל כֵּן אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pushes רבי יהודה's earlier case further, from the wedding procession to life inside the husband's home.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even words said while she is serving guests in her husband's home count as מיאון.

steps.title: Refusing even while running his errand
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי בר יהודה says that even if she says it while on an errand for her husband, there is no greater מיאון than this.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי בר יהודה went further: Even if her husband sent her to a shopkeeper to bring him something of his, and she said, 'I do not want so-and-so my husband,' there is no greater refusal than this.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי בר יהודה gives the most extreme case: she says it while she is out doing an errand for her husband.
steps.deeperAnalysis: While running his errand she is acting fully as his wife, so her words might look like a passing complaint. רבי יוסי בר יהודה says this is the strongest מיאון of all, because she is rejecting him in the middle of serving him.
steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא keeps widening מיאון. Wherever and whenever she clearly says she does not want her husband, it counts.

phrases.aramaic: יָתֵר עַל כֵּן אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר יְהוּדָה:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei bar Yehuda said more than that:
Even if her husband sent her to a shopkeeper
to bring him an item of his,
and she said: 'I do not want so-and-so my husband'
there is no greater refusal than this.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָתֵר עַל כֵּן אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the most extreme case on top of רבי יהודה's two cases.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Refusal said while on an errand for her husband is the greatest מיאון.

steps.title: The הלכה follows רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's view of רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס, and שמואל rules that the halacha follows him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס says: 'Any girl, etc.' רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: The הלכה follows רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the next line of the משנה, quoting רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס, and gives the practical ruling that the halacha follows him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The quote from the משנה is only a heading that tells us which part of the משנה is being discussed. The new information is שמואל's ruling: we follow רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס in practice.

keyTerms.meaning: Etc.: the rest of the quote is understood

phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina ben Antigonus says:
Any girl, etc.
Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
The halacha follows Rabbi Chanina ben Antigonus.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן אַנְטִיגְנוֹס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to a new line in the משנה after finishing the definition of מיאון.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The halacha follows רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס.

steps.title: Her marriage to someone else is her refusal
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא in the name of רבי יהודה בן בתירה: a minor who never refused but married another man has refused through that marriage.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: A minor girl who did not refuse, but went and married someone else: in the name of רבי יהודה בן בתירה they said, her marriage is itself her refusal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא teaching that a girl can do מיאון through her actions, by marrying another man, without saying any words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now, מיאון was done by saying 'I do not want him.' Here רבי יהודה בן בתירה teaches that marrying someone else shows just as clearly that she does not want the first husband, so it counts as מיאון.
steps.whatToRemember: מיאון can be done through actions, not only words: marrying another man is itself a refusal of the first.

phrases.english: It was taught: A minor girl who did not refuse,
and went and married someone else,

phrases.aramaic: מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בְּתִירָה אָמְרוּ:
phrases.english: in the name of Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira they said:
Her marriage itself is her refusal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a new way of doing מיאון, through action rather than words, building on the earlier definition.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A minor's marriage to another man counts as her מיאון of the first.

steps.title: What if she only got betrothed to the second man?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether a קטנה who never did מיאון, and then got betrothed (not married) to another man, has refused through that betrothal.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: if she got betrothed to someone else, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: Step 7 taught that marrying a second man counts as מיאון. Now the גמרא asks whether just getting betrothed to a second man also counts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Marriage is a strong act that clearly shows she has left the first husband. Betrothal is a smaller step, so maybe it is not enough to show she rejects him. The גמרא wants to know where the line is.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked among them (a real open question)

phrases.english: A dilemma was raised before them:
If she became betrothed, what is the law?
phrases.notes: This is the girl from the last step, who never refused her first husband, now betrothed to a different man.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the ברייתא's marriage case to a betrothal case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does betrothal to a second man count as מיאון the way marriage does?

steps.title: A ברייתא says her betrothal is her refusal
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא in the name of רבי יהודה בן בתירה rules that a קטנה who got betrothed to another man has refused through that betrothal.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: a קטנה who did not refuse, and then got betrothed to someone else — in the name of רבי יהודה בן בתירה they said: her betrothal is itself her refusal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with a ברייתא: betrothal also counts as מיאון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה בן בתירה holds that accepting קידושין from another man shows clearly enough that she does not want the first husband. So she does not need to say any words of refusal.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear (bringing a source to answer)
And she went ahead (and did something)
Her betrothal is itself her refusal

phrases.english: Come and hear:
A minor girl who did not refuse
and went and became betrothed

phrases.aramaic: מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בְּתִירָה אָמְרוּ:
phrases.english: in the name of Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira they said:
Her betrothal is itself her refusal.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: קְטַנָּה שֶׁלֹּא מֵיאֲנָה וְעָמְדָה וְנִתְקַדְּשָׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question of step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes — according to רבי יהודה בן בתירה, betrothal to another man counts as מיאון.

steps.title: A chain of questions about the רבנן and the final ruling
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the רבנן disagree with רבי יהודה בן בתירה, how far they disagree, and what the הלכה is.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: do the רבנן disagree with רבי יהודה בן בתירה or not? If they disagree, is it only about betrothal, or even about marriage? If even about marriage, is the הלכה like him or not? If the הלכה is like him, is it only about marriage, or even about betrothal?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא lays out a ladder of four questions, each one depending on the answer to the one before it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First: is there a disagreement at all? Second: if so, maybe the רבנן only argue about betrothal (the weaker act), or even about marriage. Third: who wins? Fourth: if he wins, does his view win in both cases, or only in the stronger case of marriage?

keyTerms.meaning: If you come to say (if the answer turns out to be…)

steps.confusionAlert: Notice the order flips: the רבנן's disagreement is asked 'betrothal, or even marriage,' but the הלכה is asked 'marriage, or even betrothal.' Marriage is the stronger act, so it is the easier case for him and the harder case for them.

phrases.english: A dilemma was raised before them:
Do the Rabbis disagree with

phrases.aramaic: דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בְּתִירָה אוֹ לָא?
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira or not?
If you say they disagree:
is it about betrothal, or even about marriage?

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם תִּימְצֵי לוֹמַר פְּלִיגִי אֲפִילּוּ בְּנִישּׂוּאִין:
phrases.english: And if you say they disagree even about marriage:

phrases.aramaic: הֲלָכָה כְּמוֹתוֹ אוֹ אֵין הֲלָכָה כְּמוֹתוֹ?
phrases.english: is the halacha like him or is the halacha not like him?
And if you say the halacha is like him:
is it about marriage, or even about betrothal?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: פְּלִיגִי רַבָּנַן עֲלֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בְּתִירָה אוֹ לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that רבי יהודה בן בתירה's view is known for both marriage and betrothal, the גמרא asks about the opposing view and the final ruling.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the רבנן disagree, in which cases, and whether the הלכה follows רבי יהודה בן בתירה in marriage only or also in betrothal.

steps.title: שמואל rules like רבי יהודה בן בתירה
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes שמואל: the הלכה follows רבי יהודה בן בתירה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: the הלכה is like רבי יהודה בן בתירה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings שמואל's ruling to answer the chain of questions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל states the ruling without any limit, so it is understood to cover both cases — marriage and betrothal. That answers the last questions in the chain: the הלכה follows him, even for betrothal.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא, student of שמואל, who passes on his teachings
A leading early אמורא in בבל

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical bottom line: a קטנה who marries or becomes betrothed to someone else has thereby done מיאון.

phrases.english: Come and hear,
Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
The halacha is like Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the questions of step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The הלכה follows רבי יהודה בן בתירה, with no limit, so it applies to both marriage and betrothal.

steps.title: The word 'הלכה' shows that the רבנן disagree
steps.stepSummary: Because שמואל had to say 'the הלכה is like him,' we learn that someone disagrees — the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'The הלכה' — this implies that they disagree.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a lesson from שמואל's wording, answering the very first question in the chain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You only need to say 'the הלכה follows X' when there is another opinion. So the word הלכה itself proves the רבנן disagree with רבי יהודה בן בתירה.

keyTerms.meaning: By implication; from this we can tell

steps.whatToRemember: The רבנן do disagree with רבי יהודה בן בתירה, but the הלכה follows him — even for betrothal.

phrases.english: 'The halacha' — this implies that they disagree.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference from the wording of שמואל's ruling in step 11.
steps.raayaObject: That the רבנן disagree with רבי יהודה בן בתירה.

steps.title: Was she fully married or only betrothed to the first husband?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks a new question: does רבי יהודה בן בתירה's rule apply even when she had been fully married to the first husband, or only when she had been betrothed to him?
steps.simpleTranslation: But still you should ask: is it when she had been married from the start, or perhaps only when she had been betrothed?
steps.whatsHappening: Even after the ruling, the גמרא says one question is still open: how strong was her tie to the first husband?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the question was about her act with the second man. Now the question is about her status with the first man. If she was fully married to him, maybe a betrothal to another man is not enough to show she rejects him.

keyTerms.meaning: You should ask (it remains a question)

phrases.english: But still you should ask:
is it when she had been married from the start,
phrases.notes: 'From the start' means to the first husband, before the second betrothal.

phrases.english: or perhaps only when she had been betrothed?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a further question on the rule that was just ruled as הלכה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the rule applies when she had been fully married to the first husband, or only when she had been betrothed to him.

steps.title: The story of אבדן's daughters-in-law
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a story: אבדן's daughters-in-law rebelled against their husbands, רבי sent two Sages to look into it, and the girls' words showed they rejected their husbands.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: אבדן's daughters-in-law rebelled. רבי sent a pair of Sages to check them. Some women said to them: 'Look, your husbands are coming.' They answered: 'Let them be your husbands!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a story to try to answer the question of step 13. The story ends in the next step, where we see how the גמרא uses it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The girls' reply, 'let them be your husbands,' is a way of saying 'they are not ours.' רבי had sent the Sages to look into the girls' rebellion. The proof for step 13's question depends on how the story ends.

keyTerms.meaning: They rebelled (refused to stay with their husbands)

phrases.english: Come and hear:
The daughters-in-law of Abdan rebelled,
Rabbi sent a pair of Sages to examine them.
Women said to them:
See, your husbands are coming.
They said to them:
Let them be your own husbands.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a proof attempt from a story to answer step 13's question.
steps.raayaObject: Whether רבי יהודה בן בתירה's rule applies when she was fully married or only betrothed to the first husband.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A real case brought before רבי involving אבדן's daughters-in-law (finished in step 15).

steps.title: רבי calls it the greatest refusal, and the גמרא tries to prove they were married
steps.stepSummary: רבי ends the story by calling the girls' behavior the greatest מיאון. The גמרא tries to read the story as a case where the girls were fully married.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי said: There is no greater refusal than this. Isn't it true that they were married?
steps.whatsHappening: This finishes the story from the last step. The גמרא then tries to use it to answer the question of step 13.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי treated the girls' rejection of their husbands as a real מיאון, even though they never said a formal refusal. The גמרא suggests these girls were already fully married. If so, that would prove that רבי יהודה בן בתירה's rule works even after full marriage.

keyTerms.meaning: Refusal: the way a girl married off as a minor ends the marriage
Isn't it that...? (the גמרא is offering a proof)

phrases.english: Rebbi said:
phrases.notes: This is רבי יהודה הנשיא, who sent the two Sages in the story.

phrases.english: There is no greater refusal than this.
Is it not that they were married?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the story begun in step 14 and tries to use it to answer step 13's question.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהודה בן בתירה's rule applies even when she was fully married to the first husband.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי's statement about אבדן's daughters-in-law, read as a case of fully married girls.

steps.title: No, they were only betrothed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof: the girls may only have been betrothed, not fully married.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, they were only betrothed with קידושין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the proof it just offered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the girls had only קידושין and not נישואין, the story proves nothing about a fully married girl. So this proof cannot settle step 13's question; the next step gives the ruling anyway.

keyTerms.meaning: Was betrothed with betrothal only (קידושין, not full marriage)

phrases.english: No, they were betrothed with betrothal alone.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 15.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof only. The rule itself is not rejected.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The story can be explained as a case of betrothal only, so it does not show anything about full marriage.

steps.title: The הלכה follows רבי יהודה בן בתירה, even after full marriage
steps.stepSummary: Even without a proof, the גמרא rules that the הלכה follows רבי יהודה בן בתירה, even when she was fully married to the first husband.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה is like רבי יהודה בן בתירה, even when she had full marriage with the first husband.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final ruling on the question from step 13.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof failed, but the ruling still answers the question: the rule is not limited to betrothal. Even after נישואין with the first husband, her betrothal to the second husband works the way רבי יהודה בן בתירה said.

keyTerms.meaning: The first one (here, the first husband)

steps.whatToRemember: Final ruling: the הלכה follows רבי יהודה בן בתירה, and this is true even if she was fully married to the first husband, not only betrothed.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the rejected proof in step 16 means the גמרא rules the other way. The proof was pushed away, but the הלכה still says 'even with full marriage.'
steps.whyThisMatters: This closes the whole discussion that began in step 10 with a clear practical ruling.

phrases.english: And the halacha is in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira,
even with regard to marriage to the first one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proof is rejected, gives the final ruling anyway.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי יהודה בן בתירה's rule applies even after full marriage to the first husband.

steps.title: שמואל praises רבי אלעזר for being consistent about a minor girl
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי אלעזר from the משנה. רב יהודה, in the name of שמואל, says no Sage was as consistent about a minor girl as רבי אלעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: רבי אלעזר says, etc. רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: I went over all the views of the Sages and found no one as consistent about a minor girl as רבי אלעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה, רבי אלעזר's view, and brings שמואל's comment on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי אלעזר says a minor girl's act (her marriage) is nothing. שמואל points out that other Sages treat her as married in some ways and not in others. רבי אלעזר alone keeps one simple rule all the way through.

keyTerms.meaning: Etc.: the rest of the משנה's line is assumed
Kept his rules equal, meaning he was consistent

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar says, etc.
Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
I have gone over all the sides of the Sages
and I did not find a person
who kept his standards consistent regarding a minor girl like Rabbi Elazar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: the next view in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אלעזר is the only Sage who treats a minor's marriage with one consistent rule.

steps.title: How far רבי אלעזר took his view: she can eat תרומה that evening
steps.stepSummary: שמואל shows how consistent רבי אלעזר was. He treated the girl as if she had only walked with the man in a courtyard, so she can immerse and eat תרומה that evening.
steps.simpleTranslation: For רבי אלעזר made her like a girl walking with him in a courtyard: she gets up from his lap, immerses, and eats תרומה in the evening.
steps.whatsHappening: This finishes שמואל's statement and gives a picture of how far רבי אלעזר's view goes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since her marriage is nothing, being with him is like casual time together and creates no marriage at all. So a כהן's daughter married to a non-כהן does not lose her right to eat תרומה. She only needs to immerse to become ritually pure, and she may eat that evening.

keyTerms.meaning: The holy portion of produce that only a כהן's family may eat

phrases.english: For Rabbi Elazar made her
like one walking with him in a courtyard,
and she stands up from his lap and immerses,
and eats teruma in the evening.
phrases.notes: The case is a כהן's daughter. A real marriage to a non-כהן would stop her from eating תרומה, but here there is no real marriage.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁעֲשָׂאָהּ רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר כִּמְטַיֶּילֶת עִמּוֹ בֶּחָצֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows what שמואל meant by 'consistent' in step 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Under רבי אלעזר, a minor's marriage creates no bond at all, so a כהן's daughter may still eat תרומה.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: a minor girl is not his wife at all, except that she needs refusal
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא brings רבי אליעזר's view. The husband of a minor gets none of a husband's rights, and she is not his wife in any way except that she must do מיאון.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches: רבי אליעזר says a minor's act is nothing. Her husband does not get what she finds, her earnings, or the right to cancel her vows. He does not inherit her and does not become impure for her. The general rule: she is not his wife at all, except that she needs מיאון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that spells out, rule by rule, the view that a minor's marriage is nothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This lists the usual rights a husband has and says he has none of them here. The one exception is that she still needs a formal מיאון before she can marry someone else.

keyTerms.meaning: Becomes impure for her (a כהן allowed to deal with his dead wife)

phrases.english: It is taught: Rabbi Eliezer says:
The act of a minor girl is nothing,
and her husband has no right to her found items,
nor to her earnings,
nor to annulling her vows,
and he does not inherit her, and he does not become impure for her.
phrases.notes: If he is a כהן, he may not become impure at her funeral, because she does not count as his wife.

phrases.english: The general principle:
she is not like his wife in any matter,
except that she requires refusal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא that spells out the 'her marriage is nothing' view discussed in steps 18-19.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A minor wife gives her husband none of a husband's rights; only מיאון is still needed.

steps.title: רבי יהושע: a minor girl is fully his wife, except that she can leave by refusal
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע takes the opposite view. The husband has all the usual rights, and she is his wife in every way, except that she can leave through מיאון instead of a גט.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע says: Her husband gets what she finds and her earnings, can cancel her vows, inherits her, and becomes impure for her. The general rule: she is like his wife in every way, except that she leaves through מיאון.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives the opposing view, matching the earlier list point for point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every right that רבי אליעזר denied, רבי יהושע grants. The only difference from a normal wife is how the marriage ends: through מיאון, with no need for a גט.
steps.whatToRemember: Two opposite pictures of a minor's marriage. רבי אליעזר: not a wife at all, except that she needs מיאון. רבי יהושע: a full wife, except that she can leave with מיאון.
steps.confusionAlert: Both sages agree that מיאון is involved. They argue about everything else: whether the husband has any of a husband's rights while the marriage lasts.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua says:
her husband has rights to her found items,
and to her earnings, and to annulling her vows,
and he inherits her, and he becomes impure for her.
The general principle:
she is like his wife in every matter,
except that she leaves through refusal.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר: בַּעְלָהּ זַכַּאי בִּמְצִיאָתָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite view to רבי אליעזר in the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A minor wife is a full wife in every way, except that she can leave through מיאון without a גט.

steps.title: רבי prefers רבי אליעזר's view because it is consistent
steps.stepSummary: רבי says רבי אליעזר's view seems more correct than רבי יהושע's, because רבי אליעזר is consistent about a minor girl and רבי יהושע is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי said: רבי אליעזר's words seem more correct than רבי יהושע's. רבי אליעזר kept one consistent approach to a minor girl, but רבי יהושע split his approach.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי (רבי יהודה הנשיא) judges the argument between רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע from Steps 20-21 and sides with רבי אליעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי gives a reason for his choice: consistency. רבי אליעזר treats the minor as not really a wife, and he does that all the way through. רבי יהושע is said to 'split' his approach, and the גמרא will explain this next.

keyTerms.meaning: When the name stands alone, it means רבי יהודה הנשיא, who compiled the משנה
He kept his standards equal, meaning he was consistent
Here: he split his approach, meaning he was inconsistent

phrases.english: Rabbi said:
phrases.notes: Plain 'רבי' with no name always means רבי יהודה הנשיא.

phrases.english: The words of Rabbi Eliezer appear correct
more than the words of Rabbi Yehoshua.
For Rabbi Eliezer kept his standards consistent regarding a minor girl,
while Rabbi Yehoshua split his approach.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי: נִרְאִין דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר מִדִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Judges the argument quoted in Steps 20-21
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אליעזר's view is preferred because it is consistent about a minor girl.

steps.title: In what way is רבי יהושע inconsistent?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבי meant when he said רבי יהושע split his approach.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'split his approach' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short clarifying question about רבי's words. This sets up the answer that comes right after.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי said רבי יהושע was inconsistent but did not show how. The גמרא wants to point to the exact place where his view does not hold together.

phrases.english: What is meant by 'split his approach'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of the word חָלַק in Step 22
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Where exactly is רבי יהושע's view inconsistent?

steps.title: If she is fully his wife, she should need a גט
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע calls her a full wife, yet lets her leave through מיאון. If she were truly his wife, she should need a גט.
steps.simpleTranslation: If she is his wife, she should need a גט.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question. רבי יהושע's view does not fit together: a full wife should need a גט, not just מיאון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 21, רבי יהושע said she is his wife in every way, except that she leaves through מיאון. The גמרא points out that this exception goes against the main rule. Every other real wife can leave only with a גט.

phrases.english: If she is his wife,
she should need a bill of divorce.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 23
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יהושע calls her a full wife but does not require a גט. That mismatch is his inconsistency.

steps.title: Isn't רבי אליעזר inconsistent too?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: if רבי אליעזר holds she is not his wife, why does she need even מיאון?
steps.simpleTranslation: By רבי אליעזר too: if she is not his wife, she should not need even מיאון!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the same kind of question against רבי אליעזר and suggests that he is also inconsistent.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 20, רבי אליעזר said she is not his wife in any way except that she must do מיאון. If there is no marriage at all, why should any act be needed to end it? So it seems רבי אליעזר also makes an exception.

keyTerms.meaning: Refusal: the minor girl declares she does not want her husband, and this ends the marriage

phrases.english: According to Rabbi Eliezer too:
if she is not his wife,
she should not need refusal either!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי's claim in Step 22 that רבי אליעזר is consistent
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי's statement that רבי אליעזר kept his standards consistent
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If there is no marriage at all, requiring מיאון is just as much an exception as רבי יהושע's.

steps.title: She cannot leave with no act at all
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that some act is still needed. She cannot just walk away with nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Should she then leave for nothing, with no act at all?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי אליעזר. מיאון does not show a real marriage. It is just the smallest act needed so that she does not leave with nothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי אליעזר, מיאון is only a simple statement that she does not want him. It does not mean the marriage has real force. So his view stays consistent, while רבי יהושע still treats her as a full wife who leaves without a גט.

keyTerms.meaning: For nothing / with no act at all
She will go out (leave the marriage)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי prefers רבי אליעזר. For him the minor's marriage has no real force, and מיאון is just a basic act of leaving. רבי יהושע calls her a full wife yet lets her leave without a גט, and that is inconsistent.

phrases.english: Rather, should she leave for nothing?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 25
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains what the requirement means: מיאון is a minimal act, not a sign of real marriage
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Requiring מיאון would show that רבי אליעזר also sees some marriage here
steps.terutzMaskana: מיאון is just the least action needed so she does not leave with nothing, so רבי אליעזר stays consistent

steps.title: What counts as an 'obstruction from the man'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי אליעזר בן יעקב from the משנה and asks what 'an obstruction from the man' and 'an obstruction not from the man' mean.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says, etc. What are the cases of an obstruction from the man and an obstruction not from the man?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line in the משנה and asks for a definition. This sets up two answers that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's rule depends on whether the 'obstruction' comes from the man or not. But the משנה does not say what that looks like in real life. The גמרא wants a concrete case.

keyTerms.meaning: From the man (because of the husband)
What is the case? What does it look like?

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב אוֹמֵר וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya'akov says, etc.

phrases.aramaic: הֵיכִי דָּמֵי עַכָּבָה שֶׁהִיא מִן הָאִישׁ
phrases.english: What is the case of an obstruction that is from the man
and an obstruction that is not from the man?

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכִי דָּמֵי עַכָּבָה שֶׁהִיא מִן הָאִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to a new statement in the משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A concrete definition of an obstruction from the man and one not from the man

steps.title: שמואל: it depends on why she turns down a proposal
steps.stepSummary: שמואל says: if she turns down a proposal 'because of my husband,' the obstruction is from the man. If she says 'the men are not right for me,' it is not from the man.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: If men proposed marriage to her and she said 'Because of so-and-so, my husband,' that is an obstruction from the man. If she said 'Because these people are not suitable for me,' that is an obstruction not from the man.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל gives the first definition. He looks at what reason the girl gives when someone proposes marriage to her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If she points to her husband as the reason, she shows that she sees herself as his wife. So the obstruction is 'from the man.' If her reason is only that the men are not suitable, she is not pointing to her husband, so it is not from the man.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
If they proposed marriage to her and she said:
'Because of so-and-so, my husband,'

phrases.aramaic: זוֹ הִיא עַכָּבָה שֶׁהִיא מִן הָאִישׁ.
phrases.english: this is an obstruction that is from the man.
'Because of people who are not suitable for me,'
phrases.notes: She means the men who proposed. She is turning them down, not mentioning her husband at all.

phrases.aramaic: זוֹ הִיא עַכָּבָה שֶׁאֵינָהּ מִן הָאִישׁ.
phrases.english: this is an obstruction that is not from the man.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: תְּבָעוּהָ לִינָּשֵׂא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 27
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The obstruction depends on the reason she gives when she turns down a marriage proposal.

steps.title: A second definition: a גט versus מיאון
steps.stepSummary: אביי בר אבין and רב חנינא בר אבין say: if he gave her a גט, the obstruction is from the man and the results of a real marriage follow. If she did מיאון, it is not from the man and those results do not follow.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי בר אבין and רב חנינא בר אבין both say: If he gave her a גט, that is an obstruction from the man. He is forbidden to her relatives, she is forbidden to his relatives, and she is disqualified from marrying a כהן. If she refused him, that is an obstruction not from the man. He is permitted to her relatives, she is permitted to his relatives, and she is not disqualified from marrying a כהן.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים give a different definition. They look at how the marriage ended, with a גט or with מיאון, and they list what follows from each.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Giving a גט treats the marriage as real. So she is like a divorced woman: the relatives stay forbidden, and she cannot marry a כהן. מיאון does not treat the marriage as real, so none of these limits apply.

keyTerms.meaning: He made her unfit to marry a כהן (like any divorced woman)

steps.whatToRemember: There are two ways to define 'an obstruction from the man': שמואל looks at her stated reason for turning down a proposal; the sons of אבין look at whether the marriage ended with a גט or with מיאון.
steps.confusionAlert: 'From the man' does not mean the husband did something wrong. It means the marriage is being treated as real because of him: she points to her husband, or he gave her a גט.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the practical results: a גט gives the minor's marriage the results of a real one (forbidden relatives, no כהן), but מיאון leaves no such results.

phrases.aramaic: אַבָּיֵי בַּר אָבִין וְרַב חֲנִינָא בַּר אָבִין
phrases.english: Abaye bar Avin and Rav Ḥanina bar Avin
both of them say:
If he gave her a bill of divorce,

phrases.aramaic: זוֹ הִיא עַכָּבָה שֶׁהִיא מִן הָאִישׁ,
phrases.english: this is an obstruction that is from the man,
and he is forbidden to marry her relatives,
and she is forbidden to marry his relatives,
and he has disqualified her from the priesthood.
phrases.notes: Like any divorced woman, she can no longer marry a כהן.

phrases.english: If she refused him,

phrases.aramaic: זוֹ הִיא עַכָּבָה שֶׁאֵינָהּ מִן הָאִישׁ,
phrases.english: this is an obstruction that is not from the man,
and he is permitted to marry her relatives,
and she is permitted to marry his relatives,
and he has not disqualified her from the priesthood.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּיֵי בַּר אָבִין וְרַב חֲנִינָא בַּר אָבִין דְאָמְרִי תַּרְוַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to Step 27, different from שמואל's
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גט makes it an obstruction from the man, with the results of a real marriage. מיאון makes it an obstruction not from the man, with none of those results.

steps.title: The next משנה already teaches the difference between גט and מיאון
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the explanation of אביי בר אבין and רב חנינא בר אבין. The next משנה already teaches openly that a גט creates marriage ties and a מיאון does not, so why would our משנה hint at the same thing?
steps.simpleTranslation: But it is taught later on: if a girl refuses a man, he may marry her relatives, she may marry his relatives, and he did not disqualify her from כהונה. If he gave her a גט, he is forbidden to her relatives, she is forbidden to his relatives, and he disqualified her from כהונה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the very next משנה to attack the explanation from step 29. That משנה already says plainly what אביי בר אבין and רב חנינא בר אבין said our משנה means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 29, 'an obstruction from the man' meant a גט, which brings real marriage results, and 'not from the man' meant a מיאון. But the next משנה states exactly this rule in clear words. So why would רבי אליעזר בן יעקב teach it here in a hidden way?

keyTerms.meaning: Later on, further along. Here it means the next משנה.
A girl who does מיאון, refusing the marriage her family arranged while she was a minor
Her female relatives, such as her mother or sister
He made her unfit to marry a כהן, which is what happens to a divorced woman

steps.confusionAlert: The wording quoted here will show up again word for word in step 32. Here the גמרא is only quoting it to ask a question. In step 32 the new משנה actually begins.

phrases.english: But it is taught later on:
phrases.notes: This points to the next משנה, which comes right after the גמרא finishes here.

phrases.english: A girl who refuses a man —
he is permitted to marry her relatives,
and she is permitted to marry his relatives,
and he did not disqualify her from marrying a כהן.
If he gave her a גט —
he is forbidden to marry her relatives,
and she is forbidden to marry his relatives,
and he disqualified her from marrying a כהן!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the explanation given in step 29 by showing that the next משנה already teaches the same rule openly.
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanation of אביי בר אבין and רב חנינא בר אבין that 'an obstruction from the man' means a גט and 'not from the man' means a מיאון.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה should not repeat a rule that the very next משנה states clearly. So reading רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's words as the גט/מיאון difference seems to make them repetitive.

steps.title: The next משנה is explaining this one
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that there is no repetition. The next משנה is simply explaining what our משנה said briefly.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is explaining.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the explanation from step 29. The next משנה is not a repeat; it is spelling out what our משנה only hinted at.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה said briefly that an obstruction 'from the man' brings marriage results. The next משנה explains the details: which relatives become forbidden, and that she becomes unfit for a כהן. So the explanation of אביי בר אבין and רב חנינא בר אבין still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: It is explaining (short for קָא מְפָרֵשׁ)

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common pattern: one משנה can state a rule briefly, and the next משנה can lay out its details.

phrases.english: It is explaining.
phrases.notes: He means the next משנה is explaining our משנה, so the two are not repeating each other.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 30 and keeps the explanation of step 29.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains how the two משניות relate: the later one explains the earlier one, so nothing is repeated.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The next משנה seemed to teach the exact same rule a second time.
steps.terutzMaskana: The next משנה lays out the details of what our משנה stated briefly, so the explanation of אביי בר אבין and רב חנינא בר אבין stands.

steps.title: New משנה: מיאון leaves no marriage ties, but a גט does
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה rules on the two ways a girl can leave the marriage. After a מיאון, both sides may marry each other's relatives and she may marry a כהן. After a גט, the relatives are forbidden and she is unfit for a כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If a girl refuses a man, he may marry her relatives, she may marry his relatives, and he did not disqualify her from כהונה. If he gave her a גט, he is forbidden to her relatives, she is forbidden to his relatives, and he disqualified her from כהונה.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It contrasts what happens after a מיאון with what happens after a גט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מיאון undoes the marriage from the start, so she is not treated as his former wife at all. A גט ends a marriage that counted. So even though this marriage was only valid by rabbinic law, the ties to relatives and the ban on marrying a כהן take effect.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה, marking the start of a new משנה
His male relatives, such as his father or brother
The priesthood. A divorced woman may not marry a כהן.

steps.whatToRemember: מיאון means it is as if they were never married, so nothing remains. גט means they were married and then divorced, so the relatives become forbidden and she cannot marry a כהן.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
A girl who refuses a man —
he is permitted to marry her relatives,
and she is permitted to marry his relatives,
and he did not disqualify her from marrying a כהן.
If he gave her a גט —
he is forbidden to marry her relatives,
and she is forbidden to marry his relatives,
and he disqualified her from marrying a כהן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The new משנה that step 30 quoted ahead of time now actually begins.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A מיאון leaves no ties to relatives and no ban on marrying a כהן. A גט forbids each side's relatives and makes her unfit to marry a כהן.

steps.title: First a גט, then a מיאון: she may go back to him
steps.stepSummary: He divorced her, remarried her, and then she left him through מיאון. She married someone else, who died or divorced her. She may go back to the first husband.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he gave her a גט and took her back, and she then refused him and married someone else, and was widowed or divorced, she may return to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a case where the girl left the same man twice: first with a גט, later with a מיאון. Since her last exit was a מיאון, she may go back to him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a divorced woman who married someone else may never go back to her first husband. Here, though, the final break was a מיאון. That last refusal cancels the earlier גט, so she is treated like a girl who refused, and she is not forbidden to return.

keyTerms.meaning: He took her back, he remarried her
She refused him, she did מיאון
To return to him, to remarry the first husband

phrases.english: If he gave her a גט and then took her back,
and she refused him and married another man,
and she was widowed or divorced —
she is permitted to return to him.
phrases.notes: 'Him' is the first husband, the one who gave her the גט and whom she later refused.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the basic rule of step 32 by giving a case where both a גט and a מיאון happened with the same man.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the last exit was a מיאון, she may go back to the first husband even after marrying someone else, despite the earlier גט.

steps.title: First a מיאון, then a גט: she may not go back to him
steps.stepSummary: Now the order is reversed. She refused him, he remarried her, and then he divorced her with a גט. She married someone else, who died or divorced her. She is forbidden to go back to the first husband.
steps.simpleTranslation: If she refused him and he took her back, and he then gave her a גט and she married someone else, and was widowed or divorced, she is forbidden to return to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה flips the order from step 33. This time her last exit was a גט, so she may not go back to him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the final break was a גט, and the earlier מיאון does not cancel a later גט. So she has the status of a divorced woman who married someone else, and she may not remarry her first husband. Put the two cases together: what decides is how she left him the last time.

keyTerms.meaning: A man remarrying his divorced wife after she married someone else, which is forbidden

steps.whatToRemember: In both cases the same two things happened, a גט and a מיאון. Only the order is different. Whatever came last decides: a מיאון at the end means she may go back, a גט at the end means she may not.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think that one מיאון somewhere along the way is enough to let her go back. The מיאון only helps if it was her last exit.

phrases.english: If she refused him and he took her back,
and he gave her a גט and she married another man,
and she was widowed or divorced —
she is forbidden to return to him.
phrases.notes: This is the usual ban on a man taking back his divorced wife after she married someone else (דברים 24:4).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reverse order of step 33 and reaches the opposite ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the last exit was a גט, she is forbidden to return to the first husband after marrying someone else, even though she had refused him earlier.
